skills.trigger: When evaluating chest radiographs for suspected drug-induced pneumonitis (e.g., amiodarone) or interstitial lung disease to distinguish specific patterns from other pathologies.
steps: Assess the morphology of pulmonary opacities, specifically looking for patchy, ill-defined densities rather than well-circumscribed nodules or uniform ground-glass haze.
Determine the zonal distribution by comparing opacity density in the upper zones versus the middle and lower zones; drug-induced pneumonitis often favors the mid-to-lower fields.
Evaluate symmetry to confirm bilateral involvement, distinguishing it from unilateral processes like lobar pneumonia or aspiration.
Differentiate from alternatives: Upper zone predominance suggests sarcoidosis or silicosis; well-defined nodules suggest metastases; clear fields rule out active pneumonitis.
